5 runbook section(s):

[1] connection-pool-exhaustion.md > Symptoms (score 0.4599)
Errors or log lines stating that a connection pool is exhausted, that all
connections are in use, or that acquisition timed out with many waiters queued.
Pool wait time rises sharply. Throughput collapses while CPU and memory may look
normal, because requests are blocked waiting for a connection rather than doing
work.

[2] thread-pool-exhaustion.md > Symptoms (score 0.4019)
The service stops accepting new work: log lines about a full worker pool, a
rejected-execution error, or a saturated event loop. Inbound requests are queued
or dropped with 503 responses. Already-running requests may still complete slowly.

[3] dns-and-network-failures.md > Symptoms (score 0.3992)
Intermittent or total failure to reach a dependency, with errors about name
resolution, no route to host, connection timeouts, or TLS handshake failures.
The dependency itself is healthy when reached by other clients. Failures may
cluster by client region, availability zone, or resolver.

[4] connection-pool-exhaustion.md > How to confirm (score 0.3937)
- Check pool metrics: active connections at the ceiling, waiters greater than
  zero, rising acquisition wait time.
- Correlate with downstream latency and with the caller's outbound request rate.
- If downstream latency is normal, suspect a leak; look for steadily falling idle
  connections over time.

[5] retry-storm-amplification.md > References (score 0.3927)
- AWS Builders' Library, "Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter":
